Hi Diane —

Thanks for the sample. I put together two quick, concrete examples (attached) that map your CSV rows to how our billing engine would produce invoice lines. Highlights up front:

1) Token accounting assumptions:
   - We meter on encoded tokens; typical English prompts are ~0.75 tokens/word (varies).
   - Each request is metered for prompt tokens + generated tokens.

2) Rounding & minimums:
   - We round up fractional billing units to the billing quantum (10-token quantum by default).
   - Minimum monthly floor is applied per-billing-account line item (not per-route) unless you opt into consolidated invoicing.

3) Context/session/windowing:
   - We do NOT persistently merge KV cache across disjoint requests unless your integration pins a session id. If you resume a conversation within 5 minutes using the same session id, we apply prefix KV reuse which reduces billed prompt tokens. Otherwise, each request is billed independently.

I've attached redwood_billing_examples.xlsx with worked rows. Neha from finance is cc'd to confirm the invoicing options (consolidated vs per-route). If these assumptions look good we can produce a redlined term that allows consolidated billing for your pilot.

Thanks —

Hi Keith/Diane —

Wanted to jump in with the canonical behavior so there's no surprise:

1) Minimum application:
   - The monthly minimum is evaluated at invoice time across the billing account. If total billed usage for the month < minimum, the invoice shows a single adjustment line bringing you up to the floor. So in your example (2.4K + 0 + 7.6K = 10K) you'd match the minimum exactly and pay true usage. If total had been 9.2K, we'd add a 0.8K floor charge.

2) Rounding quantum:
   - We aggregate usage per invoice period and apply the quantum rounding on the aggregated totals per billed SKU. That means we do NOT round each request individually for invoicing; we sum tokens then round to the nearest 10-token quantum upward. This limits small-request rounding blowup.

3) Cross-route consolidation:
   - Consolidated invoicing is available as an option. By default the platform emits per-route (e.g., chat vs embeddings) SKU lines. Consolidation will merge those to a single SKU for minimum/floor evaluation; it requires a term because it affects revenue recognition and discounts.

4) Session/window behavior (technical note):
   - For resumed conversations that reuse the same session id within our default 5-minute window, KV/prefix reuse reduces prompt token billing. If you need longer-lived session reuse we can configure a session retention policy, which will persist KV across requests but has cost/operational trade-offs.

I've attached the same examples but annotated to show aggregation-first rounding. Happy to run your CSV through our model and return a pro forma invoice.
